question: In a class of 30 boys of northern European descent, how many are likely to have red-green colour blindness?
answer: About 2. Roughly 8% of men of northern European descent have a red-green colour deficiency, against about 0.5% of women, because the genes for those cones sit on the X chromosome. Many never find out: they learn colour names from others and only stumble over a red line on a green chart.
move: A difference nobody mentions can still be common in the room.
ask: Who around me might be seeing a chart, a signal or a situation differently, without ever saying so?
trap: Probably none, since colour blindness is so rarely mentioned.
reference: Birch, Worldwide prevalence of red-green color deficiency, Journal of the Optical Society of America A 29(3):313–320, 2012
